children: 0310 GMT - Palm oil prices are higher in Asian trading, supported by strength in soybean oil on the Chicago Board of Trade overnight, says David Ng, a trader at Kuala Lumpur-based Iceberg X. Data from The Southern Peninsular Palm Oil Millers' Association suggests production fell 26% in Nov. 1-10, a slower-than-expected pace that still reflects improved market sentiment despite elevated Malaysian palm oil inventories, he adds. Ng expects the market to remain sensitive to production trends and rival oil price movements. Ng expects crude palm oil prices to face resistance at 4,520 ringgit a ton and find support at 4,300 ringgit a ton. The Bursa Malaysia Derivatives contract for January delivery is up 53 ringgit at 4,463 ringgit a ton. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)

0243 GMT - Nvidia's ability to sustain its pace of AI product development without CEO Jensen Huang could become an indicator of the industry's future direction, says TF International Securities analyst Ming-Chi Kuo. Huang's unique value lies not in his technical expertise alone, but in his ability to quickly align strategy, technology, organizational resources and supply chains behind ambitious product decisions, Kuo says. That leadership has given suppliers the confidence to invest and adapt to aggressive specification upgrades while pushing rivals to follow suit. If Huang emerges weakened by the ongoing controversy, Nvidia may need to gradually reduce its dependence on his personal decision-making and prepare a succession plan, Kuo adds.(megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com)

0238 GMT - Nvidia faces risks beyond replacing a chief executive, Saxo Markets chief investment strategist Charu Chanana says. Questions about the future of Nvidia's China ambitions--its key partnerships and the broader AI vision that Huang has shaped could impact the chip giant's valuation, she notes. Nvidia's technology advantage won't disappear with his departure, but the board needs to show it can protect the business while addressing governance concerns, the strategist notes. "A credible successor and clear transition plan could help steady the shares," she adds, while an abrupt removal without either would leave investors facing much more uncertainty. Nvidia's shares are down 8.6% in after-hour trading. (sherry.qin@wsj.com)

0144 GMT - A WSJ report stating that Nvidia is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang has sent the stock sliding over 8% after hours. For investors, the key question is whether the company can maintain its exceptional growth trajectory under new leadership, says Pepperstone's Chris Weston. "Nvidia still has some of the best products on the market, and that won't change anytime soon," the analyst says. But its ability to execute, sustain its competitive advantage and bring its pipeline to market now faces greater scrutiny. A CEO change could undermine the assumptions underpinning revenue growth and gross margins in the subsequent quarters, causing investors to lose confidence. And when uncertainty clouds the ability to forecast future earnings with conviction, volatility is almost invariably the result, Weston says. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)

0136 GMT - Nvidia's stock will likely remain under pressure as Jensen Huang's days as CEO could be numbered, Yorkville Ives analysts say in a note. The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia's board is preparing to oust Huang. Yorkville Ives values Nvidia at $300 a share with Huang as CEO, and at $225 without him. The analysts expect "a very fluid situation over the next 48 hours." Still, they see Nvidia getting through the turmoil and remaining a core part of the artificial-intelligence revolution. Nvidia shares fell about 8.6% to $158.76 in after-hours trading. (venkat.pr@wsj.com)

2229 GMT - Intel investors aren't pleased with the news that Nvidia's top executive could be out. Shares are down 4.3% at $59.81 post market after The Wall Street Journal reported Nvidia's board is planning to oust CEO Jensen Huang. Intel is both a partner and a competitor of Nvidia, with the two companies rivals in the semiconductor industry. However, Nvidia also invested $5 billion in Intel stock in late 2025, becoming one of the company's biggest shareholders. The two companies are also working together to develop data center and PC products using Nvidia's chips. (katherine.hamilton@wsj.com)

2213 GMT - Super Micro Computer bounced back from allegations that it was giving trade secrets to China. Its recovery could be a promising sign that Nvidia shares will also rebound, despite CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged spy. In March, Super Micro's co-founder Yih-Shyan "Wally" Liaw resigned from the board after being indicted for his alleged role in a scheme to smuggle Nvidia chips to China. Shares plummeted after his departure, but have rebounded 48% since their low on March 20. Nvidia's board is reportedly planning to oust Huang after his affair with a Chinese executive allegedly involved in espionage. Nvidia shares are down 8% after-hours, after losing 11% over the past five days. (katherine.hamilton@wsj.com)

Shares of Oracle Corp. have turned lower in the after-hours market, shedding more than 2% after the bell to trade at $125.77. The stock ended the day's regular session with an 8.8% gain, closing at $128.38. The decline comes as The Wall Street Journal reports that Nvidia is preparing to oust founder and Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. Oracle is a major Nvidia customer.(stephen.nakrosis@wsj.com)

2206 GMT - Shares of Nvidia suppliers are down after-hours as The Wall Street Journal reports that the company's board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang. Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, the Taiwanese tech giant which makes Nvidia-designed chips, is down 1.7% on the New York Stock Exchange. Micron Technology, which makes high-bandwidth memory that goes with Nvidia chips, loses 2%. Stocks of other Nvidia suppliers including ASE Technology Holding Co., ASML Holding, and Amkor Technology are trading lower as well. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

2158 GMT - Super Micro Computer shares are down following a Wall Street Journal report that Nvidia's board is preparing to oust Chief Executive Jensen Huang. The two companies have a close relationship, where Nvidia supplies chips to Super Micro, which then integrates them into server racks. As recently as late October, Super Micro announced Nvidia CPU racks that it was adding to its portfolio. Super Micro has increasingly pivoted toward selling server racks, versus individual components, making it more reliant on Nvidia. Super Micro shares are down 3.7% after hours. (katherine.hamilton@wsj.com)

2153 GMT - Nvidia's board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang over two extramarital affairs, The Wall Street Journal reports. A Huang ouster could throw Nvidia, arguably the most central company to the AI infrastructure buildout, into disarray, without a clear succession plan. The news is already being felt across the AI trade: shares in Nvidia are down 7%; Nvidia partners Oracle and CoreWeave are also down after-hours, as are Super Micro Computer and Intel. Nvidia competitor AMD, meanwhile, gains 3.8%. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

2148 GMT - CoreWeave shares fall 5.7% after-hours as The Wall Street Journal reports that Nvidia's board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang over two extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. CoreWeave is a major customer of Nvidia, which also has a 12.8% stake in the neocloud company. News of Huang's potential ouster adds to bearish sentiments around CoreWeave, whose leverage and financing needs put it at the center of market debates over the sustainability of the AI infrastructure buildout. The after-hours fall pares down CoreWeave's 25% gain during the regular trading session following a strong third-quarter earnings report. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)
